correctness.rationale: For each fixed n≥4 and Q with Q'(0)≠0, the n simple roots of z^n−1 perturb as ω_n^j+O(t), hence σ₂=1+O(t). The critical equation nz^{n−1}+tQ'(z)=0 yields n−1 distinct roots ρe^{iθ}ω_{n−1}^k+O(ρ²) from the implicit-function theorem at simple roots of its scaled limit. Since t=O(ρ^{n−1})=O(ρ³), uniform expansion of all n(n−1) distances produces h=1−ρ cos Δ_n(θ)+O(ρ²). The n zero phases modulo critical angular period 2π/(n−1) are an evenly spaced n-point grid; its farthest distance to the reference has exact range [π/n,π/(n−1)]. The linear directions q1=1 and q1=e^{-iπ/n} attain both coefficient endpoints. All quantifiers and remainders are fixed-n,Q, and no numerical experiment is used as proof.

originality.rationale: Teng Zhang establishes the global sharp variance inequality in Theorem 1.2 but not its first nonzero defect for perturbed regular-binomial equality examples. The 2011 source formulates global equality rigidity as a conjecture; Miller analyzes local extrema of the different Chebyshev-radius Sendov objective. The independent local Puiseux phase law and its sharp endpoint directions were not found in inspected primary papers or targeted exact/equivalent searches.
residual_risks: The multiple-root Puiseux expansion is classical and a local Sendov extremality paper not found in search could conceivably contain an equivalent angular coefficient after renormalization. In particular the full 1993 Vâjâitu–Zaharescu treatment was not accessible; the available description concerns the differently normalized Sendov problem.
The leading law is directionwise, not uniform as Q'(0) approaches zero or as degree increases; degenerate first-derivative directions require another Newton polygon.
No global equality rigidity at exponent two or uniform neighborhood around the full binomial orbit is proved.

value.rationale: The regular-binomial family is the sharpness and conjectured equality model of the recently settled Borcea 2-variance inequality. The first deficit in generic coefficient directions is nonanalytic because all critical points coalesce, and the relevant max-min functional makes its leading coefficient genuinely phase dependent. The theorem computes that coefficient for every transverse Q direction, gives an exact sharp degree-dependent interval and realizes both endpoints, thereby providing a meaningful local equality-stability boundary absent from the global source. The result does not claim a paper-sized or uniform global stability theorem.
